tasks.notes: Documents-only amendment of packages/eng-harness/docs/plans/0013-column-workflow.md. Plan task T2 (calc harness.column_select with golden and property tests) was written on origin/feat/b281-harness-gt2-calc-harness-column-select and stopped at 313 counted lines against max_changed_lines 200. Measure that branch yourself (the counted-lines rule of the playbook, per file, against its merge base with origin/build/v1). Lead decision D-12 allows a budget within the 400-line cap when the content is one coherent unit: if the counted content is one calc module with its registration and no padding, set T2 max_changed_lines to the measured count plus a margin of about 10 percent (at most 380), with a YAML amendment comment (B-459) that states the measurement; if you judge it is two separable units, split it into T2 and T2b by the rules of a split instead (own files, tests_first files inside each task, covers keeping every acceptance criterion, depends_on; later tasks that depended on T2 then depend on the last part). Also check T2's files list covers every file the branch really needed (for example the calc lock, the calcs package __init__, the kinds module): add only what the calc genuinely requires. The pull request body line is `Plan-Task: none (spec and plan)`.

The plan's front-matter risk is the binding Risk line (amendment B-453 raised this plan to carry r2: read the plan's `risk` and use exactly that set, whatever the registry says). The branch exists on origin with the stopped writer's commits (never reviewed): fetch it into the worktree, merge origin/build/v1 (no rebase) and finish it against plan T2 as amended by B-459. Verify test-first: the first commit must be `test:` with the tests_first tests failing at the merge base for the right reason; if the existing history cannot pass test-first, rebuild the same content on a fresh branch `feat/b281-harness-gt2-calc-harness-column-select-v2` with a `test:` first commit (lead decision D-22) and report the new branch name clearly in your summary so later roles use it. Engineering calc: hand-check every golden `derivation`, X/Y and the verticality tolerance (its source must be the spec or the design basis).
